the enzyme is an endonuclease with 3'- and/or 5'-nuclease activity.
the enzyme is a lysosomal enzyme, an endonuclease, a 5'- and 3'-nucleotydohydrolase and has a transition temperature at which the activation energy changes.

the isolation and characterization of lysosomal acid deoxyribo-nuclease from vervets monkey livers.
the isolation of lysosomal acid DNases from primate livers.
the properties of lysosomal acid DNases from primate livers.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
primate lysosomal DNase is an enzyme that is able to degrade DNA into small polymers, which can be further degraded to mononucleotidic products by 3'- and/or 5'-nucelotidohydroses.
the enzyme is a highly active, endonucleolytically acting, acid phosphatase, with a high affinity for its substrate.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the enzyme is a lysosomal enzyme, and that the lysosomes are the site of DNA degradation.
